patch_description:
The old program was fundamentally broken: it effectively fell back to `fixed_reorder` (its recursive machinery misused `itertuples` attribute access, dropped/renamed columns via "original_index", and returned an empty `column_orderings` list, so per-row orders were invalid). It also asserted shapes that failed once `col_merge` changed column counts, and its reward model (squared field lengths) doesn't match the actual character-prefix-Trie objective.

Fix: replace the editable block with a correct, bounded implementation. It (1) serializes every row exactly like the evaluator (`"".join(fillna("").astype(str))`), (2) builds up to three cheap candidate orderings — a global frequency-ranked order (score = Σ len(v)·c·(c−1)), a shallow conditional-partition order that picks leading fields by pair repetition inside value groups, and a count-only variant — (3) scores each candidate with the exact ideal Trie reuse (sum of adjacent LCPs over sorted serialized strings, computed via C-speed binary search on prefix slices, capped by a total-character budget), and (4) returns the best candidate's DataFrame plus valid per-row column orderings. All cells, rows, and columns are preserved verbatim (only permuted per row), missing values and mixed types are handled via object dtype, and `col_merge` is honored via the base class `mererging_columns` when supplied.
